explanation: Hasekura Tsunenaga crossed the Pacific to Mexico, then the Atlantic to Spain. While he was away, the shogunate banned Christianity, and by his return in 1620 his mission had failed.

claims.text: In 1615 the samurai Hasekura Tsunenaga, leading an embassy from Japan, was received by Pope Paul V in Rome.
Hasekura's embassy sailed across the Pacific to New Spain (Mexico), then across the Atlantic to Spain.
The Tokugawa shogunate banned Christianity in 1614, while Hasekura was abroad.
Hasekura's mission failed to secure the trade agreement it sought.
